## 90-Day Launch Plan: $35 Stainless Garlic Press (Amazon US, FBA)

### Start with the unit economics
The fees below are placeholders until you confirm them in the Revenue Calculator. Landed cost is my assumption, so replace it with your real figure.

| Per unit | Value | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Price | $34.99 | Your call |
| Referral fee | $5.25 | Last-known 15% for Kitchen; confirm |
| FBA fulfillment fee | $5.00 | PLACEHOLDER; depends on size tier and weight |
| Storage + returns allowance | $1.00 | PLACEHOLDER |
| Landed cost | $8.00 | ASSUMPTION |
| Prep and packaging | $0.50 | ASSUMPTION |
| **CM before ads** | **$15.24** | |
| **Break-even ACoS** | **43.6%** | $15.24 ÷ $34.99 |

If all 1,000 units sell, $6,000 in ads works out to $6.00 per unit, which leaves about $9.24 CM per unit after ads. So the real budget control is ad spend per unit sold. Set a launch stop-loss at $10 per unit for two weeks in a row, and aim for under $4 once sales are steady.

Price is the bigger risk. $35 is a premium price for a garlic press. Before launch, check the price and rating of the top 20 results for "garlic press." If you're at twice the median price, the listing has to justify it (one-piece stainless vs. zinc alloy, easy cleaning, a clear comparison chart). Otherwise weak conversion breaks the ad math.

### Days −14 to 0: Foundation
- **Brand Registry** comes first. It unlocks Vine, A+, Sponsored Brands, and Brand Analytics.
- **New-seller programs**: check New Seller Incentives and the FBA New Selection program. The last I knew, they offered credits and fee rebates on new parent ASINs. Confirm the current terms.
- **Listing**: Title = Brand + Garlic Press + Stainless Steel + top differentiator. Each bullet leads with the result (crushes unpeeled cloves, rinses clean, won't rust), then the spec that proves it. Answer what competitors' reviews and Q&A complain about: ginger, dishwasher safety, how hard it is to squeeze, rust.
- **Images**: white-background main image, in-hand scale shot, unpeeled-clove demo, cleaning shot, comparison with generic zinc presses (no competitor brand names), what's in the box. Add video if eligible.
- **Claims**: "18/8 stainless" and "dishwasher safe" need supplier specs or test reports on file. Don't say "antibacterial" (that's a pesticide claim), and never say "FDA approved." Send food-contact questions to regulatory counsel.
- **Backend terms**: garlic crusher, mincer, presser, ginger press, common misspellings. No competitor brands.
- **Inbound**: send all 1,000 units to FBA (Vine units ship from FBA stock) unless capacity limits block it. Compare the inbound placement options.

### Days 1–30: Launch (~$2,700 ads, ~$90/day)
- **Vine**: enroll up to 30 units on day one. The last-known fee was $200 for up to 30 units, with lower tiers for fewer units; confirm. Cost ≈ fee + 30 × (landed + FBA) ≈ $590 using the placeholders.
- **Request a Review** on every eligible order. The package insert carries care instructions and a support contact only. Don't tie a review request to a star rating, and don't offer any incentive.
- **Campaigns**:
  - SP Auto discovery: low bids, with each of the four targeting groups bid separately
  - SP Exact: "garlic press," "garlic crusher," "stainless steel garlic press," "garlic mincer"
  - SP Phrase/Broad expansion on those roots, with negative exact on the Exact terms
  - SP Product targeting on ASINs you beat on rating or material
- **Bid ceiling**: 0.40 target ACoS × 10% assumed CVR × $34.99 = $1.40. If suggested bids run far above that, fix conversion or price before adding budget.
- **Price**: hold $34.99. If you need a lever, use a 10–15% coupon and model it with the current coupon fee (Amazon changed that fee structure recently; confirm). Don't show an inflated "was" price.

### Days 31–60: Harvest and tighten (~$2,000)
- Harvest weekly. Move terms with 3+ orders at ACoS ≤ 35% to Exact. Add a negative for any term with 20–30 clicks and no orders (2–3 ÷ your CVR).
- Add Sponsored Brands video on category terms once you have enough reviews to show (my rule of thumb is 15+).
- If the ASIN is eligible, test the main image or title in Manage Your Experiments.
- **Reorder is the decision that matters most.** Assume 12 units/day, a 60-day lead time, and a standard deviation (σ) of 5 units/day. Safety stock = 1.65 × 5 × √60 ≈ 64. Reorder point = 12 × 60 + 64 ≈ 784. You reach that about two weeks after hitting 12/day. Confirm real sales per day and lead time by day 30 and place the PO then. If you wait, you run out of stock before day 90 and lose the ranking you paid for.

### Days 61–90: Profit mode (~$1,300)
- Move spend to Exact performance campaigns and Sponsored Brands, and cut discovery to a maintenance level. Targets: ACoS 25–30%, TACoS under 12%, ad spend under $4 per unit.
- Pause branded campaigns as a test before adding defense budget.
- Send negative review themes to product/QA.

### Weekly scorecard
CM per unit after ads, ad spend per unit, ACoS vs. the 43.6% break-even, TACoS, unit session percentage, reviews and rating, Featured Offer %, weeks of cover.

### What I need from you
Your landed cost, packaged dimensions and weight, supplier lead time, and Brand Registry status. I'll replace the placeholders with confirmed, dated numbers and rerun the plan.

## Conversion Drop: 14% → 8% in Two Weeks

A drop that big (a 43% relative fall) that fast usually has one specific cause. Amazon doesn't publish its ranking formula, but sales velocity and organic rank tend to move together, so treat this as urgent.

### Step 0: Protect margin today
At the same CPC, ACoS rises by 14 ÷ 8 = 1.75×, so a 20% ACoS becomes 35%. Compare that with your break-even ACoS (contribution margin before ads ÷ price). Until you find the cause, reset bids with this formula: max CPC = target ACoS × current ad conversion rate × price. For example, 0.25 × 0.08 × $29.99 = $0.60, down from $1.05 at 14%.

### Diagnostic checklist (work from the top down)

**1. Is the drop real?**
- [ ] Same metric in both periods: Business Reports unit session percentage, at the same parent/child level, with B2B handled the same way
- [ ] Raw counts: did units fall, or did sessions jump? 8% on double the sessions is a traffic problem, not a listing problem
- [ ] Sample size: at 30 sessions a day, a few orders swing the rate

**2. Is another seller getting your sales?**
- [ ] Check Featured Offer % by day. A new seller, a hijacker, or a suppressed Featured Offer (often price-related) gives you sessions without your units
- [ ] Make a test buy from any unexpected seller and keep screenshots

**3. Price and promotions**
- [ ] A coupon, deal, or Prime-exclusive discount ended, or the strike-through reference price disappeared
- [ ] A repricer moved your price
- [ ] Competitors cut prices or ran deals (did the window overlap Prime Big Deal Days or the weeks right after?)

**4. Delivery promise and stock**
- [ ] Low stock or regional stockouts are pushing delivery dates out or dropping Prime in some ZIP codes
- [ ] A variation child is out of stock and showing as the default
- [ ] Units are stranded or inbound shipments are delayed

**5. Reviews and badges**
- [ ] Average rating fell, a new 1–2 star review now sits at the top, or a critical Q&A appeared
- [ ] A "Frequently returned item" warning appeared, the Amazon's Choice badge was lost, or a variation family broke and no longer pools reviews

**6. Listing integrity**
- [ ] The live title, bullets, main image, and A+ still match your last approved version (other contributors or Amazon can overwrite them)
- [ ] A+ or video is suppressed, or there's a listing quality or policy alert in Account Health
- [ ] Check the mobile view, where most shoppers see only the first image, the price, and the delivery date

**7. Traffic mix**
- [ ] New or broadened campaigns (auto, broad, product targeting, Sponsored Display audiences) are adding low-intent sessions
- [ ] The search term report shows new terms with many clicks and zero orders
- [ ] In Search Query Performance (brand owners only), compare click, add-to-cart, and purchase share by query, before vs. after
- [ ] Off-Amazon traffic (influencers, social, email) is sending shoppers who aren't ready to buy

**8. Competition**
- [ ] A new page-one competitor has a lower price, a better rating, or faster delivery
- [ ] Competitors are running product-targeting ads on your detail page

### Action plan

**Days 1–2: Triage**
- Put 30 days of daily sessions, units, Featured Offer %, price, inventory, rating, and ad spend in one sheet. Mark the day the drop began and match it against every change: yours, the repricer's, ads, stock, reviews.
- Reset bids as above, and pause discovery campaigns that spend without getting orders.

**Days 3–7: Fix the cause you found**

| Cause | Fix |
|---|---|
| Featured Offer lost to another seller | Make a test buy. Use Report a Violation only with evidence. Handle unauthorized resellers through distribution agreements and counsel, never with IP complaints you can't back up |
| Promo ended or price moved | Model any coupon or price change in the unit-economics sheet first, and stay inside the fair pricing policy |
| Stock or delivery speed | Expedite replenishment and recalculate the reorder point from your measured lead time |
| Listing overwritten | Restore it through Brand Registry and open a case with before/after screenshots |
| Negative reviews | Send the defect, or the gap between what buyers expected and what they got, to product/QA. Fix any listing copy that set the wrong expectation. Use Vine if eligible. No incentives, and don't ask only happy buyers for reviews |
| Traffic mix | Add negatives for irrelevant terms and cut bids on weak placements. Judge results on orders and margin, not sessions |
| Competition | Sharpen the comparison image and bullets around your real advantage. Cut price only if the margin supports it |

**Days 8–30: Confirm and prevent**
- Track daily: unit session %, Featured Offer %, in-stock rate, TACoS, and contribution margin per unit after ads
- Test future image or title changes in Manage Your Experiments (if eligible) instead of editing the live listing
- Set alerts for Featured Offer % below baseline, rating changes, any seller's price change, and weeks of cover below your target range
- Log the root cause, fix, and date so you can diagnose the next drop in an hour

### Send me
Daily sessions and units for 30 days, Featured Offer %, price and promotion history, daily inventory, and the search term report. I'll tell you which cause on this checklist it is.
